description: The Nuclear Facilities Attack Database (NuFAD) is a global database recording assaults, sabotages and unarmed breaches of nuclear facilities, built by START researchers at the University of Maryland after finding that systematic open-source data on terrorist threats to nuclear facilities was lacking. From numerous historical anecdotes, unsubstantiated reports and vague references they identified the most relevant cases, and the resulting database contains 80 cases from open sources covering 1961 to 2014, with a full source listing on the site. The initial beta version offers brief summaries of each incident, an interactive map and timeline, and filters to remove cases not meeting the user's criteria; future versions were planned to add detail. The creators are Gary Ackerman and James Halverson, described in a 2016 chapter in the book Nuclear Terrorism: Countering the Threat. Coverage is global. Access: web tool, free; no licence is stated and no bulk download was seen. Caveats: beta, open-source cases only, and last covering 2014. It suits security threat and resilience studies of nuclear plants, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
